# Parasites

> *How do life cycles explain where a parasite is caught, where it lives, and how it is found?*

::: {.callout-note}
## In preparation
This chapter will follow the layout of [*Gram-positive cocci*](gram-positive-cocci.qmd). The plan:
:::

| Part of the chapter | Plan |
|---|---|
| The group in one sentence | Eukaryotic organisms that live on or in a host: single-celled protozoa and many-celled worms (helminths) |
| Sorting key | Protozoa versus helminths; life cycle (infective and diagnostic stages); definitive and intermediate hosts |
| Main organisms | *Plasmodium* (mosquito and human stages), *Giardia* (cysts in water), *Toxoplasma* (cats and other hosts), *Ascaris* (eggs in soil) |
| Supporting organisms | *Entamoeba*, *Cryptosporidium*, hookworms, *Strongyloides*, tapeworms, *Schistosoma* |
| Later in the course | Malaria, gut parasites and others in the organ blocks; antiparasitic drugs in pharmacology |
